articles.summary: NEW DELHI: IndiGo has extended the cancellation of flights to and from Riyadh until October 31, while services to Jeddah, Dammam and Madinah will remain
articles.body: NEW DELHI: IndiGo has extended the cancellation of flights to and from Riyadh until October 31, while services to Jeddah, Dammam and Madinah will remain suspended until October 27, amid heightened security concerns in Saudi Arabia following a deadly attack at King Fahd International Airport in Dammam.In a travel advisory posted on X, the airline said the decision was taken after assessing the evolving security situation.“Travel Advisory. In view of the evolving security situation and following a careful assessment, IndiGo flights to and from Riyadh will remain cancelled until 31 October 2026 (inclusive), while flights to and from Jeddah, Dammam and Madinah will remain cancelled until 27 October 2026 (inclusive),” the airline said.IndiGo said it was monitoring developments closely and coordinating with the relevant authorities to assess the situation.“The safety and well-being of our customers and crew remain our highest priority,” the airline said, adding that affected passengers were being informed through the contact details provided at the time of booking.The airline advised passengers to check their flight status on its official website before leaving for the airport and apologised for the inconvenience caused by the cancellations.The announcement comes after an attack at King Fahd International Airport in Dammam on Wednesday evening left two people, including an Indian national, dead and eight others injured, according to Saudi authorities.The Indian Embassy in Riyadh said on Thursday that one Indian national was among those killed, while two other Indian nationals were injured. The embassy said it was gathering further details and contacting the affected families.Saudi Arabia's General Authority of Civil Aviation identified the deceased as a Saudi citizen and an Indian resident. It said the injured included two Indian residents and nationals and residents of other countries. The injuries ranged from minor to severe, and the injured were receiving medical treatment in hospitals.The authority said airport operations had resumed and air traffic had returned to normal following the incident. Efforts to assess the damage and ensure the safety of passengers and airport staff were continuing.IndiGo's announcement follows a similar move by Akasa Air, which earlier extended the suspension of its flights to and from Riyadh and Jeddah until October 27, citing security concerns in the Middle East.You use AI every day. articles.title: Israel orders Hebron lockdown, prepares to shut entire West Bank after shooting from Friday
articles.summary: Israel has directed its military to prepare for a complete closure of the occupied west bank on Friday following a deadly shooting incident near the city
articles.body: Israel has directed its military to prepare for a complete closure of the occupied west bank on Friday following a deadly shooting incident near the city of Hebron that left several people injured.Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office said security forces had been instructed to immediately seal off Hebron and make arrangements to shut down the entire west bank from Friday, according to news agency AP.The orders followed an announcement by the Israeli military that its forces had killed two gunmen and foiled what it described as a “terror attack”.Two gunmen killed, at least five injuredIsraeli soldiers shot dead two men who the military alleged had carried out an attack near Hebron in the occupied west bank on Friday morning. At least five people were injured, some of them critically.According to the army, the two men were armed with an M16 rifle and a handgun. The military said its forces had prevented an attack targeting Israeli civilians but did not disclose the alleged target or identify the deceased and injured individuals.Following the incident, Israeli forces established roadblocks and imposed restrictions on movement in Palestinian towns across the surrounding area.Emergency responders said they reached the scene near Yehuda junction while gunfire was still being reported. The injured were evacuated to hospitals in Israel for treatment.According to the emergency services, two men in their 20s sustained gunshot wounds to their lower limbs, while another person was unconscious and seriously injured.“We arrived at a difficult scene while shooting was still taking place in the area,” said Tzuriel Edri, a member of the emergency response team.Authorities said an investigation into the incident was underway.Attack raises security concerns ahead of Israeli electionThe shooting comes days before Israeli voters are scheduled to cast their ballots next Tuesday in an election that could determine whether Benjamin Netanyahu secures another term as prime minister or the country enters a new political phase.The election is taking place three years after the Hamas-led attacks on Israel that triggered the war in Gaza.The Israeli government has warned of possible attacks by what it described as the country's “enemies” in the run-up to the vote.Following Friday's incident, far-right Israeli national security minister Itamar Ben-Gvir argued that the attack underscored the need to impose further restrictions on Palestinian movement in the West Bank.“The lives of the residents of Judea and Samaria, of the settlers, the lives of the soldiers, the lives of the police officers, the lives of our fighters are a million times more important than freedom of movement,” Ben-Gvir said.Ahead of the anniversary of the October 7, 2023, Hamas-led assault, Netanyahu had also alleged that Hamas could launch an attack against Israel to influence the election outcome. articles.title: Two Israeli soldiers killed in attack by suspected Palestinian gunmen in West Bank
articles.summary: The two attackers were shot dead after a gun battle outside Hebron, four days before Israel's general election.
articles.body:
Two Israeli soldiers have been killed in a shooting by two suspected Palestinian attackers in the occupied West Bank, the Israeli military says.

Three Israelis were wounded in the attack before the gunmen were shot dead, officials say. It happened at a military checkpoint at the entrance to the city of Hebron.

In response, Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he had ordered the military to prepare for a full lockdown of the West Bank, beginning later on Friday.

The attack comes at a time of high tensions, with extremist Jewish settlers targeting Palestinians during the annual olive harvest, and Israel's general election taking place in four days time.

Footage verified by the BBC shows an intense gun battle between soldiers and the gunmen.

The Israeli military said it had found a large quantity of ammunition in the attackers' vehicle, and that they believe the gunmen had intended to carry out a much larger attack on the nearby Route 35, but ran into the checkpoint - so instead decided to open fire there.

Unverified CCTV footage shows two gunmen exit a car armed with what appears to be a handgun and an assault rifle and start firing on soldiers at the checkpoint, before coming under return fire.

The attack has already begun to influence the ongoing election campaign, with Netanyahu - who has built his campaign on the promise of security - saying that his Likud party would cancel campaign events which had been set for Friday morning.

He also visited the site of the attack on Friday afternoon, saying Israel is ready for "extensive action" in the West Bank.

His far-right coalition partner Bezalel Smotrich called for Israel to launch a campaign in the West Bank "exactly like in Gaza or Lebanon," while far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir called for Israel to dismantle the Palestinian Authority.

On Thursday, Foreign Minister Israel Katz accused opposition leaders of undermining the government by criticising Netanyahu's warnings of an attack ahead of the election, saying they would be "responsible" for any future attack on the country.

Opposition chiefs, including frontrunner Gadi Eisenkot and former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, offered their condolences to those injured and praised the troops who killed the attackers.

The Israeli military said it had begun raids on the homes of the attackers, while Smotrich said he had ordered the demolition of several Palestinian buildings adjacent to the site of the attack.

It is common practice for Israeli forces to demolish the homes of Palestinians who are suspected of carrying out attacks on Israelis.

The West Bank was already expected to be placed under lockdown for the election on Monday and Tuesday, according to Israeli media.

At least 96 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli forces or settlers in the West Bank since the start of the year, according to the UN.

Four Israelis, both security forces and civilians, have been killed by Palestinians there over the same period, the UN says.

articles.title: James Bond: Jack Lowden and Callum Turner to screen test this weekend, reports say
articles.summary: Callum Turner and Jack Lowden "appear to be in the mix" of actors doing screen tests for the role.
articles.body:
Callum Turner, Jack Lowden and Josh O'Connor are among the actors thought to be taking part in final auditions to play James Bond, according to reports.

Screen tests are said to be taking place this weekend, possibly as early as Friday, according to the Hollywood Reporter , with between three and five actors understood to have reached the last stages of the process.

The finalists are said to be taking part in auditions with three components - stunts, camera presence and dialogue.

Deadline reported the screen tests had been due take place in early October, but had been delayed by scheduling conflicts, while Variety said Turner and Lowden "appear to be in the mix" to replace Daniel Craig.

British actors Aaron Taylor-Johnson and James Norton were previously connected to the role, while Irish actor Paul Mescal's name had also been thrown into the mix.

Other actors now appear to be in the frame, but reports on the current casting situation vary.

Variety suggested Slow Horses star Lowden may now be edging ahead, while Masters of the Air star Turner was speculated about earlier this year, with some fans suggesting his wife Dua Lipa could sing the Bond theme song.

Sources told Deadline that at least four final screen test offers have been made, and while unconfirmed, "three of the four expected to test are Jack Lowden, Callum Turner and Josh O'Connor".

O'Connor is best known for playing Prince Charles in The Crown, and for starring in 2025's Wake Up Dead Man: A Knives Out Mystery, with Craig.

Jack O'Connell had been thought to be in the mix, but sources said this may no longer be the case, while Euphoria and Wuthering Heights Star Jacob Elordi is not thought to be testing.

Other stars who were previously linked with the role include The King's Man star Harris Dickinson, along with SAS: Rogue Heroes' Jack Barton.

Deadline said: "Even with the tests wrapping next week, there is no timeline for when a final decision will be made."

Amazon MGM Studios, who now control the Bond franchise, announced in May that the casting process was under way, but had no further comment at the time.

In August, Amy Pascal, one of the next film's producers, told Deadline the "end of the year is a good bet" for possible news on who would be playing Bond.

"We are being really, really methodical. Having worked with Barbara Broccoli at the studio, I mean, Daniel Craig is a hard act to follow," she said.

"And it's got to be something really different that is a stirring and exciting and different."

The BBC's Lizo Mzimba reported in September that "for a series where the stakes are so high, no expense is spared in ensuring that the film team know exactly how each auditionee will come across on screen".

He added: "As the 007 team themselves have explained in the past: 'Bond screen tests are elaborate affairs involving hair and make-up, costumes, sets, and other actors'."

Only six actors have ever played novelist Ian Fleming's British Secret Service agent 007 in the official film series - Sean Connery, Roger Moore, George Lazenby, Timothy Dalton, Pierce Brosnan and Daniel Craig.

The last announcement of a new Bond was in 2005 with Craig, who last starred in the role in 2021's No Time to Die, directed by Cary Joji Fukunaga.

During the equivalent stage of the audition process two decades ago, Superman actor Henry Cavill was widely thought to have also been in the running.

"They told me I was close," Cavill told the Happy Sad Confused podcast in 2022. "They told me it was ultimately down to, and this is what I've been told, it was just down to me and Daniel, and I was the younger option.

"They obviously went with Daniel and I think it was an amazing choice to go with Daniel," he said. "I probably wasn't ready at the time and I think Daniel did an incredible job over the past movies, so I'm happy they made that choice."

The forthcoming film, reportedly out in 2028, will be directed by Dune's Denis Villeneuve , with Peaky Blinders creator Steven Knight writing the script .

Knight told Zoe Ball on Greatest Hits Radio in September that the first draft of the script was completed.

Amazon bought MGM for $8.5bn (£6.3bn) in 2021 , which included the rights to distribute James Bond, and they are reported to have paid at least $20m (£14.9m) more for the rights to creatively control Bond's future.

Pascal and David Heyman are producing the film, while Tanya Lapointe is executive producer.

Knight's final words on the film were about how much he was enjoying working on it.

He told Ball: "I'm absolutely loving doing it. It's an honour to be asked. And believe it's going to be so good. I really do believe it's going to be amazing."

articles.title: Bradford Council fund to help businesses switch to green vehicles
articles.summary: Council leader Stephen Place says it will help businesses counter the rising cost of fuel.
articles.body:
A £2m fund has been launched to help businesses switch their vehicles to greener vehicles, Bradford Council has announced.

Reform UK council leader Stephen Place said it would help businesses counter the rising cost of petrol and diesel as well as modernise their fleets.

The funding is part of Bradford Council's Clean Air programme, which will allow businesses to apply for up to £16,000 in support.

Announcing the fund at the Scale Up Bradford event on Tuesday, Place said it would help businesses invest in cleaner, more efficient technology to "future proof their operations for years to come".

Earlier this month, Place said he was committed to scrapping Clean Air Zone (CAZ) charges as it had a negative impact on businesses.

He accepted the move would have "quite a lot of legalities surrounding it" but said the council would "work to run it out naturally".

Funded by the Labour government, the Zero Emission Grant Programme will be targeted at small businesses, charities and organisations, according to the Local Democracy Reporting Service.

Businesses will be able to apply for up to £16,000 to improve heavy-duty vehicles and £4,500 for light-duty vehicles.

Bradford Council said the fund would provide practical support to help businesses remain competitive while adapting to new vehicle technologies.

"We want to help organisations to upgrade their fleets and position themselves for future success," said Place.

"I hope that this will appeal to tradies, they are the people out there every day keeping the nation moving."

Petrol and diesel prices have risen significantly since the US-Israel war with Iran.

Currently the average price of petrol in the UK is 173.2p per litre, while diesel costs 199.9p per litre.

Mark Casci, of West Yorkshire Chamber of Commerce, welcomed the plans and said a lot of businesses were looking to "decarbonise" their vehicles.

"Every large business with a fleet is looking at this issue very carefully, it is very much on their agenda," said Casci.

"It is the right thing to do and what customers want. It is driven by customer demand as well as moral responsibility."

articles.title: UK's biggest bank Barclays to cut 5,000 jobs, and puts it on AI efficiency; here's what presentation to employees said on job cuts
articles.summary: Barclays is cutting around 5,000 jobs.
articles.body: ​Barclays is cutting around 5,000 jobs. The move comes as the UK's largest bank expands its adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) to improve efficiency and cut costs. The banking group has already eliminated 1,000 positions and expects to cut another 4,000 roles by the end of 2026. The reductions represent around 5% of its global workforce and form part of an ongoing cost-cutting programme.​According to a New York Times report, the bank released a presentation this week noting that about 60% of the job cuts will affect support functions, including software developers. Barclays cited “organisational simplification and technology change efficiency” as part of its efforts to streamline operations, with AI expected to play an increasing role in its business.​What Barclays' presentation said about job cuts​In the presentation, Barclays outlined the job reductions to employees and investors after reporting its quarterly financial results. The bank said the cuts were part of a broader programme of organisational changes, technology investments, and efforts to simplify its operations.​The bank's cost reductions are focused primarily on its UK retail banking business, although other divisions, including investment banking, are also affected. Some back-office functions supporting the UK business are based in India, where the bank expects a significant share of the job cuts.​Barclays is nearing the end of a three-year cost-cutting programme to improve operational efficiency. The bank expects its efficiency measures to deliver an additional £1.1 billion in savings in 2027.​The bank has also said it is continuing to build its workforce and develop the skills needed to support its business strategy and changing customer needs.​Barclays CEO says AI is 'the icing on the cake'​Barclays Group chief executive C.S. Venkatakrishnan said the job cuts were part of the bank's efforts to simplify and improve its business through technology investments.​Speaking to reporters, he acknowledged AI's growing role in banking but said the technology was not the only factor behind the changes.​“AI has an important role to play and may have a more important role to play in the future,” Venkatakrishnan said.​“We will employ AI at scale,” he said. “But AI is the icing on the cake not the cake.”​He added that banks needed to build the necessary infrastructure before they could fully benefit from AI adoption.​The announcement comes as financial institutions increasingly explore automation to reduce the time and resources required for routine administrative, programming and support tasks. However, employees across the sector remain concerned about how much AI will replace existing jobs.​Barclays is not the only bank cutting jobs amid AI adoption​Barclays' announcement follows similar moves by other financial institutions exploring technology-led efficiency measures. In May, Standard Chartered said it planned to eliminate more than 7,000 jobs over four years, with support functions among the affected areas.​HSBC and Danske Bank have also flagged AI-related job reductions this year, highlighting the pressure on banks to assess how automation could change their workforce requirements.​Russ Mould, investment director at AJ Bell, told the BBC that banks would need to weigh potential cost savings against security and customer service considerations before implementing AI more widely.​Unite general secretary Sharon Graham criticised Barclays' approach, accusing the bank of using AI to justify workforce reductions.​“Employers should be focussed on upgrading employees' skills so that they remain employed as new technology changes the workplace. Instead, Barclays is guilty of taking a short-term, kneejerk approach,” she said.​Will Howlett, a financial analyst at Quilter Cheviot, said the reductions illustrated how automation could reshape banking operations.​“Banks have spent heavily on technology for years, but we are increasingly reaching the point where that investment translates into fewer people being required to run the business,” he said.You use AI every day. articles.title: Rare plaques discovered in hallway of family home in Shaftesbury
articles.summary: The plaques by Renaissance artist Francesco Xanto Avelli hung in a family home for years.
articles.body:
Two rare plaques have been sold for £100,000 at auction in a "once-in-a-generation" moment in art history.

For years, a family in a small Shaftesbury home had enjoyed glancing up at the two pieces of art in their hallway - which depicted a scene of Cyrus the Great, founder of the Achaemenid Empire .

It was only when they emailed a picture to Wiltshire-based auctioneers Woolley and Wallis that they realised the plaques had been created by famed Renaissance artist Francesco Xanto Avelli who lived between 1487 and 1542.

John Axford, chairman of Woolley and Wallis, said: "The rediscovery of these two Xanto plaques is the sort of event that happens perhaps once in a generation."

The auction, which took place on 22 October, marked the first time since 1884 that the 16th-century plaques, which are both signed by the artist, have been brought to market.

A UK-based buyer bought the plaques for a combined total of just over £100,000 including fees.

Axford added: "Hidden from public view for more than 140 years, they [the plaques] represent a thrilling survival from one of the most celebrated groups of Renaissance maiolica ever created.

"Their impeccable provenance, tracing back to Sir Andrew Fountaine's legendary collection and carrying a fascinating connection to the Medici court in Florence, only adds to their significance."

The two plaques form part of a series of around 39 maiolica plaques painted in 1536 by Xanto, who was born in Rovigo, in the Veneto region of Italy.

Elsewhere, two plaques from the painter's Life of Persian King Cyrus are held in the Louvre collection in Paris.

The two plaques arrived in England with Sir Andrew Fountaine of Narford Hall in Norfolk.

It is thought they were purchased when he went on The Grand Tour - a long-distance trip through Europe once undertaken by wealthy, upper-class young men - around 1714.

The plaques remained in the Fountaine collection for generations until the family decided to dispose of them in an auction in 1884.

The plaques were bought by General Augustus Henry Lane Fox Pitt Rivers of Pitt Rivers Museum in Oxford.

They passed down through the Pitt Rivers family, by descent, to the present owners in the West Country.

Jeremy Lamond, head of valuations at Woolley and Wallis, said: "We are delighted to have discovered the plaques through a routine valuation enquiry, which proved to have been undiscovered for over 140 years."

articles.title: A New York family owned half of a private road beside its 45-acre property; after relatives blocked it with tree trunks, the state's highest court ruled a 1,500-member club had gained title to it
articles.summary: A New York family that owned half of a private road beside its 45-acre property has lost ownership of that portion to a neighbouring recreational club
articles.body: A New York family that owned half of a private road beside its 45-acre property has lost ownership of that portion to a neighbouring recreational club with around 1,500 members. The two sides had shared the road for decades, but their relationship deteriorated in 2021 when members of the family blocked part of it with tree trunks. The disagreement eventually reached New York's highest court, which ruled on Thursday that the club had gained ownership because it had used and maintained the road for many years.The dispute concerns Godfrey's Pond Road in Genesee County, which runs between two properties. According to details of the case available on Justia, one belongs to the Genesee County Fish and Game Protective Association, a club established in 1909 that owns around 200 acres. The other is a 45-acre property belonging to Capri Dix and her husband, William Dix, who use their land for recreation.The road had an unusual ownership arrangement. The club had owned its western half since 1932, while the Dix family and earlier owners had held the eastern half since at least 1949. Despite this division, both sides had used the road for years. For the club, it was particularly important because it was the only route available to its members, emergency vehicles and delivery services.For much of that time, the relationship between the neighbours had been friendly. Capri Dix was once a member of the association, and several of her relatives had also belonged to it. The families had a long history of sharing the road and using the surrounding area. However, disagreements over access to the Dix family's land eventually brought that relationship to an end.Tree trunks turn disagreement into court battleThe trouble began when the Dix family reportedly became concerned that club members were entering their property without permission.By 2021, the disagreement had become serious. Members of the family placed tree trunks across the eastern half of Godfrey's Pond Road, preventing the association from using that section as it had done previously. Tensions increased further after an encounter between the two sides required police intervention.The club had earlier offered to purchase the family's half of the road, but the proposal was rejected. With the disagreement unresolved, the association approached the court.Instead of asking only for permission to continue using the road, the club claimed that it had already become the legal owner of the disputed section.Why club said the road belonged to itThe association's argument was based largely on what it had done to maintain the road over several decades. According to the court records, the club had regularly cleared snow, repaired damaged sections, patched the surface and carried out paving work across the entire road.Its members had also used the route daily for years to reach the club's property. Twenty-one association members lived permanently on the grounds, while others visited for recreational activities.The club argued that its long history of maintaining and using the road showed that it had treated the entire route as its own.Under New York law, someone can sometimes become the legal owner of land that originally belonged to another person if they have openly used and controlled it as their own for a long enough period.This rule, called adverse possession, does not mean that anyone who regularly uses another person's property can claim it. The nature of that use, including whether it happened with the owner's permission, also matters.But the Dix family argued that the club had been allowed to use the road because the two sides had maintained friendly relations for generations.Family's long connection with the clubThe court records showed that the relationship between the Dix family and the association went back many years. Capri Dix's grandmother, great-aunt, and great-grandmother had regularly ridden horses along the road and on trails within the club's property. Her great-grandfather, Vincent Frens, was also described as a close friend of several association members.There was evidence that Frens had allowed the club to collect gravel from his land for road repairs. He had also permitted members to hunt on his property.The Dix family also maintained that they and their relatives had regularly used the entire road, including the section now claimed by the association.The club, however, argued that its years of maintaining the route and using it as its own were sufficient to establish ownership.What New York's highest court decidedThe association initially won its case in a lower court. The Dix family challenged that decision, but an appeals court also ruled in the club's favour.The dispute then reached the New York Court of Appeals, the state's highest court. On Thursday, the court upheld the earlier decision, ruling that the association had established its ownership claim.Five judges supported the outcome, while two disagreed. The majority considered the club's decades of maintaining and using the entire road sufficient to support its claim. It also found that the family had not presented enough evidence to require a trial.However, Judge Jenny Rivera disagreed. In a dissent supported by Chief Judge Rowan Wilson, she argued that the long history of cooperation between the neighbours raised questions about whether the club had used the road with permission.She believed those questions should have been examined at trial before ownership was transferred. The majority nevertheless upheld the ruling in the association's favour.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Taiwan billionaire Chang Yung-fa left a $3 billion fortune behind; his foundation is now seeking a share of the estate in a family inheritance battle
articles.summary: Taiwanese billionaire Chang Yung-fa, the founder of the Evergreen shipping and aviation empire, left behind a fortune estimated at more than $3 billion
articles.body: Taiwanese billionaire Chang Yung-fa, the founder of the Evergreen shipping and aviation empire, left behind a fortune estimated at more than $3 billion when he died in 2016. Nearly a decade later, his estate remains at the centre of a legal dispute involving his family and a charitable foundation he established. The Chang Yung-fa Foundation is now seeking money from the estate, arguing that the late businessman had promised to leave his wealth to charitable causes. Its claim has reopened a long-running inheritance battle despite a court ruling that upheld his will.Why is Chang Yung-fa’s $3 billion estate back in disputeAccording to Crain Currency, the Chang Yung-fa Foundation announced that it would seek a share of the late billionaire’s estate after learning that some assets had been transferred into a joint account held by the executors of his will.The foundation believes Chang had intended his remaining wealth to support charitable work rather than pass entirely to individual family members. It has therefore taken legal action against the people responsible for administering his estate, arguing that his earlier promises to donate his money should be honoured.The renewed dispute is significant because the courts had already addressed a major part of the family’s inheritance battle. The latest case concerns whether Chang’s statements about donating his wealth created a separate legal obligation that must be fulfilled, even though his will named a sole beneficiary.How did the original inheritance battle beginChang, who died in January 2016, built Evergreen into a major shipping and aviation business. His business interests and substantial personal wealth eventually became the subject of a bitter dispute among his children after the terms of his will became known.According to TaiwanNews, Chang signed a sealed will in 2014 that designated his youngest son from his second marriage, Chang Kuo-wei, as the sole inheritor of his personal assets. The will covered savings, shares and real estate valued at approximately NT$14 billion, equivalent to around $433 million at the time of the report.The document also indicated that Chang Kuo-wei would succeed his father as chairman. However, the decision angered other members of the family, particularly Chang Kuo-cheng, the third son from Chang’s first marriage, who challenged the will in court.The disagreement extended beyond the distribution of personal wealth and affected relationships within the wider business family. Tensions also surrounded the leadership of Evergreen’s aviation interests, with disagreements among the brothers contributing to changes in the group’s corporate leadership.The courts upheld the will after years of litigationThe legal challenge against Chang’s will continued for several years. According to Taiwan News, Chang Kuo-cheng argued that his father had not been in an appropriate condition to make the will and questioned whether the document had been properly signed and witnessed.The initial court decision favoured Chang Kuo-wei. Subsequent appeals also failed to overturn the ruling, and Taiwan’s Supreme Court dismissed the challenge on 14 August 2024.That decision confirmed the legal validity of the will and brought the principal dispute over its authenticity to an end. However, it did not necessarily resolve every issue surrounding the administration and distribution of the estate.The distinction is central to the foundation’s latest action. Its claim is based not simply on who was named in the will but on whether Chang had separately committed himself to donating money to the foundation after his death.What evidence does the foundation cite for Chang’s charitable intentionsThe foundation maintains that Chang repeatedly expressed his intention to leave his remaining wealth to charitable causes. According to Caproasia’s report of May 2026, the organisation believes his statements reflected a genuine commitment to supporting people in need.One important piece of evidence is Chang’s 2012 oral autobiography, titled Iron Will and a Gentle Heart: 33 Attitudes to Life. The foundation has pointed to passages in the book in which he discussed donating his remaining money to the organisation.The foundation has also referred to his public statements and recorded remarks. In its view, these were not merely general expressions of support for charity but evidence of a promise concerning what should happen to his wealth after his death.The legal question is whether those statements established an enforceable agreement to make a gift upon death. Such an arrangement would need to be distinguished from the instructions contained in the formal will, which had already been upheld by the courts.The foundation argues that Chang’s charitable intentions should be respected. The opposing side disputes whether his statements created a legally binding obligation.The latest lawsuit puts the estate’s administration under scrutinyThe foundation initially brought its case against the four executors responsible for administering Chang’s will. It is seeking NT$1 billion, or approximately $30 million, rather than simply asking the court to reconsider the entire inheritance arrangement.According to Crain Currency, the foundation’s decision to pursue the claim followed its discovery that part of Chang’s estate had entered the executors’ joint account. The movement of those assets prompted the organisation to seek legal recognition of what it considers Chang’s outstanding charitable commitment.The case also raises questions about the responsibilities of the executors. They must administer the estate in accordance with the legally recognised will while responding to the foundation’s separate claim.The executors’ position differs from that of the foundation. They maintain that the will is valid and that the foundation has not established a legally binding agreement requiring the estate to make the requested payment.The proceedings have continued despite the 2024 ruling on the will. The foundation’s claim has introduced a separate legal question that must be considered alongside the established inheritance arrangements.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Burnham suggests stocking up on tinned food and bottled water
articles.summary: The prime ministers says unexpected events seem to be becoming more common and it was wise to prepare.
articles.body:
The prime minister has advised people to stock up on tinned food and bottled water in order to be prepared for emergencies.

With storms battering the UK, and in the wake of online disruption caused by a major security flaw, Andy Burnham said "unexpected events seem to be becoming more and more common".

The government has drawn up recommendations for households to have three days' worth of bottled water and tinned food to deal with a crisis such as a war, an online attack or a natural disaster.

Burnham added: "It's not about panic buying... It's about just taking sensible measures to have enough in the house to tide you over should there be a difficult situation."

At Labour's conference last month, Housing Secretary Angela Rayner joked that her emergency box would include a bottle of wine.

She said she'd include: "Mascara, concealer, I don't know, a bottle of Sauvignon Blanc, a tin of baked beans because you've gotta have some baked beans, and I like a good tin of custard as well so I think that'll keep me going for a while."

Asked whether he agreed with her, Burnham told BBC Radio 5 Live's Matt Chorley: "Well, I'm not sure a bottle of wine is your best first port of call if you're in a slightly crisis situation, but it probably helps when you've done the hard work.

"But I'll stick to the basics I think -- I do like my beans, so I have plenty of those in the cupboard, and soup.

"I think those are the kind of things that I would recommend people to have, as well as Twiglets, I'm not sure I can get by for too long without those."

Last month, the National Audit Office (NAO) warned Britain's food supply chain is at risk given the growing threat of cyber-attacks and the climate crisis and said the Department for Food, the Environment and Rural Affairs (Defra) had not done enough in recent years to improve supply chain resilience.

The chief executive of the Cold Chain Federation, which represents firms transporting temperature-controlled foods, also told the BBC the UK is being targeted by Russian cyber-hackers who "know that there are pinch points in the food supply system".

Speaking at a wildfire resilience summit in Liverpool, Burnham denied the government had failed to properly prepare, saying: "No, we're having the conversation with people about being better prepared because we're living in a world where unexpected events seem to be becoming more and more common.

"Obviously, weather events, and we're in a situation today where the UK is facing storms and obviously, we feel for the people without power in Cornwall right now.

"It is just having those supplies in the house to get you through those moments. So we are having that conversation about resilience."

Why should I stockpile and what will I need?

A checklist drawn up by the government recommends having nine litres of water per person – enough for three days – along with non-perishable food such as tinned meat and vegetables or dried fruit.

The government suggests having an FM radio, either battery or wind-up. During a national crisis, the BBC would prioritise broadcasting news, as well as health and safety information. In the event of a severe power cut, FM radio will be the best way to receive these updates.

The list also suggests hand sanitiser, wet wipes and toiletries, food for any pets, supplies for any babies, a torch, blankets, a charged power bank for devices, cash in case payment systems collapse, a first aid kit and copies of important documents.

Earlier, Treasury minister James Murray told BBC Breakfast he has not yet followed the government's guidance on stockpiling supplies to prepare for a crisis.

He said he had a stockpile of coffee, but pointed out that neighbouring countries including Ireland, France and the Netherlands had given the same guidance "for quite a long time".

He added: "I'm not going to pretend I've followed all that advice myself yet."

Speaking on the same programme, Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said she was "stocked up for the week at any time".

She said the previous Conservative government had issued similar advice on preparing for emergencies, but added: "What I'm more concerned about is that it doesn't look like [the government] are explaining what the risks we are under are, and what they are doing about the big things.

"Families can stock up but what's going on with defence, the cyber attacks, the hybrid warfare? The money to look after the country has not been forthcoming."

articles.title: Windsor Bray Film Studios given permission for major expansion
articles.summary: The Royal Borough of Windsor and Maidenhead has approved plans for building six more sound stages.
articles.body:
A historic film production facility has been given the green light to expand.

On Thursday, Royal Borough of Windsor and Maidenhead gave Amazon, the owner of Bray Studios, a unanimous permission to build six more sound stages at the premises in Windsor.

The tech giant took over the studios in 2024, after the previous owner had got planning permission to expand them in 2022.

Kiera Head-Lewis from the Berkshire Film Office in Slough, which helps facilitate filming across the county, said the development also supported local businesses, crew and talent to find jobs in the industry.

The studios was previously used by the Hammer Films company.

The British Film Commission (BFC) previously said it "recognises that the studio benefits from Amazon MGM's commitment" and welcomed its "ambition to support employment opportunities for both the local community and more widely across the UK sector".

Head-Lewis said they "get a whole load of different requests with the close links to London, just being off of the M4".

"It's become a great place to film in Berkshire because we have such a wide variety of filming locations - we have the urban but then we also have the countryside which is something that London can't necessarily compete with."

She said some of the productions they had facilitated include crime drama Mobland, which filmed in Reading, and the new Marvel series VisionQuest.

"That was a very big production, we worked with them over around five to six months and they filmed in Slough," Head-Lewis said.

She said they were always in touch with "a whole range of companies", which created links to help them "get the foot in the door".

"With local career and talent - we're always receiving job opportunities that we share with our with our networks to get them into the industry," she added.

articles.title: After spending more than 20 years rebuilding a Spitfire fuselage in his UK garage, an aviation enthusiast died in 2025; his final project, made from historic aircraft parts, sold for £18,000 in October
articles.summary: For more than 20 years, a garage in the British town of Newport Pagnell housed the partly rebuilt body of a historic Spitfire aircraft.
articles.body: For more than 20 years, a garage in the British town of Newport Pagnell housed the partly rebuilt body of a historic Spitfire aircraft. Its owner, Peter Arnold, had spent decades collecting aircraft remains and putting together pieces of aviation history. But he never got to see his final project sold. Arnold died in 2025, aged 83, and on October 8, this year, the unfinished aircraft fuselage fetched £18,000 at an auction in England.According to a report by The Independent, Arnold was widely known among aviation enthusiasts as “Mr Spitfire”. His garage contained the reconstructed fuselage of a Supermarine Spitfire F Mk 22, identified as PK519. But the fuselage was only the main body, assembled using surviving wreckage and parts recovered from other Spitfires.The aircraft was not always hidden away inside the garage. Arnold sometimes moved it onto his driveway, allowing members of the public to have a closer look. In 2003, when asked about keeping the unusual project at home, he said, “I just like it being here.”The fuselage remained at Arnold's home for more than two decades. Following his death, it became part of an auction handled by Dominic Winter Auctioneers in Cirencester.Childhood fascination became a lifelong hobbyArnold grew up near RAF Northolt, a Royal Air Force station in England. Aircraft were a source of fascination from an early age, and that interest continued during his school years.At Harrow County Grammar School, he admired a stained-glass window showing the Supermarine S6B racing aircraft. The aircraft had been flown by John Boothman, a former student who won the Schneider Trophy in 1931.Outside school, Arnold spent time visiting old aircraft crash sites. He would cycle to these locations and examine the remains left behind. During one such visit, he discovered Spitfire XVI RW386.His childhood interest eventually developed into decades of collecting and research. Arnold travelled internationally to examine more than 260 Spitfires and spent approximately 50 years locating and documenting over 350 aircraft crash sites.Arnold also worked in automotive engineering, including at Aston Martin, which helped him travel farther in search of historic aircraft remains.In 1973, he recovered two Seafire fuselages, SX336 and SX300, from a scrapyard in Warrington. Other aircraft parts followed as his collection expanded.The Spitfire that eventually reached his garageOne of Arnold's final projects involved PK519, an aircraft that had already passed through several stages of service before its remains became part of his collection.According to Vintage Aviation News, PK519 was ordered in 1943 and completed as a Spitfire Mk 22 with a Griffon 61 engine. It reached an RAF maintenance unit in September 1945, shortly after the Second World War ended.After spending time in storage and undergoing modifications, the aircraft joined No. 615 Squadron of the Royal Auxiliary Air Force at Biggin Hill in August 1949.Its service eventually ended as the squadron moved to newer aircraft. By 1954, PK519 had been withdrawn and placed in storage.The aircraft was subsequently used as a ground target on the Salisbury Plain military ranges, where aircraft carried out demonstration attacks.Aviation historian Peter Foote discovered its remains in 1966. Arnold visited the range in 1977 and recovered some surviving components. Other parts reached him years later through fellow collectors.By then, PK519 was no longer anything close to a complete aircraft. Rebuilding its main body meant bringing together pieces that had survived in different places.What buyers received at the auctionArnold used original panels from other Spitfires to help reconstruct the fuselage, fitting them around wooden supports.The finished sections included a cockpit window assembly and a transparent Perspex canopy. The instrument panel fitted inside was a paper representation intended for display.The auction lot also included five original Griffon propeller blades, painted black with yellow tips. Other surviving components included metal sections, undercarriage parts and wreckage associated with PK519.Arnold had registered the aircraft with the Civil Aviation Authority as G-SPXX in May 2012, although the reconstruction remained unfinished.According to Dominic Winter Auctioneers, “Peter was the doyen of Spitfire historians, and we hope that his collection will be appreciated for many more years to come.”The fuselage sold for £18,000 on October 8. Other items from Arnold's collection included an aircraft instrument panel containing original instruments and an RAF sector clock dating to 1941.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Meghan Markle 'deeply distressed' as father Thomas is investigated over alleged child sexual abuse material
articles.summary: Markle Sr. has denied the allegations, calling them 'sick lies' and 'the worst thing anyone could accuse me of.'
articles.body:
Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, has said she is "deeply distressed" by the news that her father, Thomas Markle, is under investigation over claims he possessed images containing child sexual abuse in his home.

The images were reportedly found in his home in the Philippines after he returned to the U.S. in May, Philippine officials said.

Thomas Markle has denied the allegations, calling them "sick lies" and "the worst thing anyone could accuse me of."

In a statement through her spokesperson, Meghan Markle has said that she is "deeply distressed" by the news, and that she was first made aware of the claims by the Met Police in 2018.

"I am deeply distressed at the news that has come to light in the last 24 hours, and my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed," Meghan's statement said. "In 2018, a letter was sent to the Metropolitan police and Royalty and Specialist Protection. That letter was subsequently shared with me. It made troubling and disturbing allegations against my father and I was given assurances that these were being investigated.

"I hope it can now be understood that, despite certain media publications' distortion over the years, any distance from my father, and my choice to not allow him to have contact with our children, was for one reason: to protect them.

"I trusted that the authorities were doing the same for other families.

"Although the breadth of what has now been uncovered is more sickening than one could ever imagine, my sincerest hope is that justice will be fully served and that the priority remains the safety and protection of innocent children."

The allegations, reported by Mail Online , said Thomas Markle is under investigation after being reported by his son, Thomas Markle Jr.

In a statement to Mail Online , the elder Markle said: "I'm shocked, I'm hurt and I'm very upset that my son is making these accusations against me. I could never do what I'm being accused of. It's the worst thing anyone could accuse me of.

He added: "It's just a bunch of lies. It's sick. I have no idea why Tom [Markle] is trying to destroy me with these lies."

Yahoo has contacted the Met Office and authorities in the U.S. and the Philippines for comment.

articles.title: In 2012, Lauren Conrad bought a Beverly Hills penthouse for $1.35 million and stripped it back to the studs; four years later, her rebuilt 3,200-square-foot home sold for $2.8 million, more than double the price
articles.summary: Reality TV star turned fashion designer Lauren Conrad has sold her fully renovated Beverly Hills penthouse for $2.8 million (£1.9 million).
articles.body: Reality TV star turned fashion designer Lauren Conrad has sold her fully renovated Beverly Hills penthouse for $2.8 million (£1.9 million). This is more than double the $1.35 million she paid for the home four years earlier, according to property records reported by the Los Angeles Times. Conrad, best known for appearing on the MTV reality series The Hills, first bought the duplex apartment in 2012 for $1.35 million. After buying it, she stripped the 3,200-square-foot property back to its basic structure and carried out a major redesign of both its layout and interiors. The work was documented at the time by Architectural Digest. The property went on the market in late 2015 for $3.2 million. It found a buyer in early 2016 for $2.8 million.Down to the studs rebuildWhen Conrad bought the penthouse, it had outdated fixtures and a floor plan divided into separate rooms. Rather than make only small cosmetic changes, she chose to carry out a complete renovation, stripping the home back to its basic framework. The renovation opened up the layout, creating a smooth flow between the living, dining and entertaining areas. High ceilings were exposed, and traditional architectural details were added to balance the modern, open-plan design. According to Architectural Digest, Conrad personally managed the interior design work. She chose custom finishes and reclaimed materials to give the home a look suited to her style. The project turned the two-storey space into a city home with several bedrooms, custom woodwork, hardwood floors and updated utility systems.Key features of the penthouseThe redesigned 3,200-square-foot home has a large, open-plan living area built around a vintage fireplace mantel. Large floor-to-ceiling windows and sliding glass doors line the main living spaces. They open directly onto private outdoor terraces with views across the Los Angeles basin. The upper floor holds the main bedroom suite, designed as a private retreat within the home. It includes a separate sitting room, a larger walk-in dressing area with built-in storage, and a bathroom finished in marble. The bathroom has a freestanding soaking tub and two sinks set into a double vanity. The penthouse also includes two guest bedrooms, three bathrooms, a second living lounge and a modern kitchen. The kitchen has custom cabinets, marble worktops and commercial-grade appliances.Financial returns and real estate strategyThe $2.8 million sale price gave Conrad a gain of $1.45 million before renovation costs and closing fees. Real estate analysts note that major structural renovations require a large upfront investment. However, complete renovations in high-value areas such as Beverly Hills can bring higher returns when finished with premium materials and features. The sale also reflects Conrad's continued activity in Southern California's housing market. Over the past decade, she has bought, renovated and resold several expensive homes across Los Angeles and Orange County. These include detached single-family homes in Pacific Palisades and coastal properties in Laguna Beach. Property records cited by the Los Angeles Times confirm that Cary Glenn of Main Street Properties represented Conrad in the sale. The buyer was represented by the real estate agency The Agency.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

articles.title: Nant Gwynant software 'genius' on holiday in Malta fell to death from hotel balcony
articles.summary: A post-mortem examination found a "substantial level" of alcohol in Kieran Hughes blood.
articles.body:
A software engineer may not have known he was falling to his death from a balcony, an inquest has heard.

Kieran Hughes, 25, from Nant Gwynant, Gwynedd, died in the early hours of 11 July, 2025, while on holiday in Malta with three friends.

A post-mortem examination by Maltese authorities found there was a "substantial level" of alcohol in his blood.

The inquest at Caernarfon Coroner's Court heard there was no evidence of third-party involvement, and coroner Elizabeth Dudley-Jones concluded his death was an accident.

His dad, Alan, said the family endured "heartache all day, every day". Hughes' friends said he had been a high achiever, "a legend and a genius".

In July 2025, Hughes and his friends went to St Julian's in Malta and stayed at the Cavalieri Art Hotel.

On 10 July, the court was told, they left the hotel at about 19:00 BST, went to dinner, a casino and elsewhere, drinking beer, cocktails and limoncello.

At about 04:15 on 11 July, a member of the public went into the hotel to say a man was lying on the ground outside.

Police were called and found a man "in a pool of blood" who looked "lifeless".

Police went to room 603, above where Hughes' body was found, and tried to wake his friend, Osian Jones, who was asleep in a "state of intoxication" and smelled of alcohol.

The pair had been sharing a room, while the other two friends were in a different room.

The inquest heard Jones did not wake up until about 06:30, but after investigations there were no indications of third-party involvement in Hughes' death.

There was no disarray in room 603, the inquest heard, and CCTV showed the pair returning to their room holding on to each other.

"It does not seem that there was any animosity between Kieran and Mr Jones," Dudley-Jones said.

There were no reports of shouting or arguing.

CCTV captured Hughes' fall about 48 minutes after he returned to his room.

An autopsy concluded he died from multiple injuries following blunt force trauma due to a fall from height.

No apparent resistance injuries were found, indicating it was possible "he was not even aware he was falling from the balcony".

The inquest heard it was probable Hughes and his friend went to sleep, and Hughes, in a state of "severe drunkenness" went outside - possibly because he felt unwell or wanted air.

Dudley-Jones told Hughes' family, who attended the hearing, his death was a "complete tragedy" and he was "an amazing man".

She added: "I have not enjoyed this inquest... this one, I have to say, it is very moving."

In a statement read to the inquest by the coroner, Hughes' father Alan said the family encountered "hurdle after hurdle" in dealing with the Maltese authorities and said they experienced "heartache all day, every day".

articles.title: An Illinois couple replaced their ordinary grass lawn with a native garden; five years later, more than 130 native plant species and a parade of animals have transformed their backyard
articles.summary: When Crystal Fritz and James Reed McGuire moved from a Chicago condominium to Highland Park, Illinois, in late 2020, they had little experience with
articles.body: When Crystal Fritz and James Reed McGuire moved from a Chicago condominium to Highland Park, Illinois, in late 2020, they had little experience with outdoor gardening. Rather than maintain a conventional suburban lawn, the couple decided to create a native garden that could provide food and shelter for birds, bees and other wildlife. Over the next five years, they gradually replaced most of the grass across their quarter-acre property, learning through trial and error which plants belonged in the region. Their garden now contains more than 130 species native to northern Illinois and attracts an array of wildlife, including foxes, bats, butterflies, birds and fireflies. What began as a personal effort to make their yard more wildlife-friendly has also encouraged neighbours to reconsider their own gardens.How the couple began transforming their lawnMcGuire, an avid birdwatcher, wanted their new home to offer more than a conventional stretch of grass. The couple had previously grown herbs and flowers in containers on their Chicago balcony, but neither had much experience managing a garden on a larger property.They began researching native plants and how to create a habitat suited to local wildlife. Their first attempts were not always successful. They initially struggled to remove the existing grass by hand and used a packet of wildflower seeds that included plants unsuitable for their region.The setbacks encouraged them to learn more about local species and how to establish a garden that would provide resources for wildlife throughout the growing season.The technique that helped them replace the grassOne method that helped the couple expand their garden was sheet mulching, a technique used to suppress existing grass before planting. They cut the grass short, covered it with cardboard and added mulch over the top. As the underlying grass died, the area could be prepared for new planting.Instead of converting the entire yard at once, Fritz and McGuire worked in stages, gradually extending the native garden across their property. After five years, the remaining grass was largely limited to paths through the garden.Their experience also taught them the importance of choosing plants native to northern Illinois rather than relying on generic wildflower mixes.More than 130 native plant species now grow in the gardenThe garden includes more than 130 plant species native to northern Illinois, combining flowering plants, grasses, sedges, shrubs and trees. Among the species McGuire has documented are prairie smoke, wild columbine, blue flag iris, purple coneflower, butterfly milkweed, foxglove beardtongue, bottle gentian and black-eyed Susan.Little bluestem, Pennsylvania sedge and prairie dropseed add variety, while shrubs such as serviceberry, winterberry and red osier dogwood provide further structure. Trees including eastern redbud, American sycamore and pagoda dogwood form part of the planting.This variety creates different sources of food and shelter for wildlife, while flowers blooming at different times of the year help sustain pollinators across the growing season.Foxes, bats, butterflies and more than 100 bird species visitThe change is reflected in the wildlife the couple have observed. McGuire reported recording more than 100 bird species visiting the garden, including migratory birds that use it as a stopover. Bees and butterflies are frequent visitors to its flowering plants.Other animals recorded around the property include red foxes, rabbits, raccoons, skunks, opossums, bats, squirrels and field mice. The couple have also reported occasional visits from deer and coyotes.Fireflies have become another attraction. Families sometimes walk past the property so children can see them, while the dense vegetation offers wildlife a more varied habitat than a conventional grass lawn.The garden has earned wildlife habitat recognitionThe couple's work has received formal recognition from conservation organisations. In 2023, their garden was designated a Certified Wildlife Habitat by the National Wildlife Federation. Openlands, a Chicago-area conservation organisation, has also certified the property as a sustainable native habitat and ecosystem.The National Wildlife Federation's certification programme recognises gardens designed to provide wildlife with essential resources, including food, water, cover and places to raise young. The designation recognises the habitat features of the garden rather than representing a scientific measurement of how much local biodiversity has increased.The property has also featured on local sustainable garden tours, allowing visitors to see how native landscaping can work in a residential setting.Neighbours have begun rethinking their own gardensThe transformation has extended beyond the couple's property. Their garden initially stood out in a neighbourhood where conventional lawns were more common, and some neighbours were sceptical about the appearance of the new planting.Over time, however, people began stopping to ask questions, photograph the garden and learn about native species. In an October 2026 interview with People, Fritz described how a neighbour who had initially objected to what he considered weeds eventually grew to appreciate the garden.Younger families have also shown interest, with some asking how they could introduce native plants into their own yards. The couple's experience illustrates how a small residential garden can become a starting point for conversations about wildlife-friendly landscaping.Fritz has encouraged people interested in native gardening to begin with a manageable area rather than attempt a complete lawn conversion immediately. A container, a small corner of a yard or a patch planted for pollinators can provide a starting point.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Computer hidden behind a fridge in a hotel room in Japan had been sending lakhs of phishing emails to steal card details since over a year; used hotel Wi-Fi; here's how it was traced
articles.summary: Japanese police have arrested a Chinese couple after a computer, tucked away behind a refrigerator in a Kobe hotel room, was discovered running a massive
articles.body: Japanese police have arrested a Chinese couple after a computer, tucked away behind a refrigerator in a Kobe hotel room, was discovered running a massive email scam for more than a year. In this unusual cybercrime case, the hidden machine was connected to the hotel’s public Wi-Fi and sent out an estimated 480,000 phishing emails designed to deceive recipients and steal their credit card credentials.The suspects, identified as 39-year-old Ye Jiafeng and his 39-year-old wife, Shen Qi – both local residents – were taken into custody not only for operating the hidden system but also for allegedly using stolen credit card data to finance high-value shopping sprees, Tom’s Hardware reported (via Hackread). Both individuals now face multiple criminal charges, including computer fraud, trespass and fraudulent obstruction of business.Hidden behind a fridge: How the phishing PC ranThe operation began on May 15, 2025, when Ye hooked up the computer to the hotel’s wireless internet network and concealed it behind a refrigerator in one of the guest rooms. Once secured in place, the machine was managed remotely, removing any need for either suspect to return to the room for physical maintenance.Reportedly, operating quietly from its hiding spot, the computer fired off roughly 4.8 lakh fraudulent messages. When investigators finally seized the unit, they found a database containing around 2.4 million email addresses queued up for future phishing runs. The outgoing messages impersonated legitimate credit card issuers, directing recipients to counterfeit landing pages to harvest payment details and security numbers.How the hidden PC was tracedThe covert setup would likely have continued running unnoticed if an observant recipient had not taken action. After receiving one of the phishing messages, the recipient analysed the email’s technical metadata and spotted the hotel’s IP address. The individual alerted the hotel management, prompting staff to search the premises.Upon finding the computer concealed behind the refrigerator, the hotel reported the device directly to law enforcement authorities. Police investigators are continuing their inquiry to determine whether the couple planned and controlled the operation themselves or acted as ground-level operators for a larger criminal syndicate.74 smartphones and 10 million Yen in fraudulent purchasesAuthorities allege that Ye and Shen loaded stolen credit card details onto smartphones to make fraudulent retail purchases across Kobe. A subsequent raid of the couple’s home uncovered a cache of 74 mobile phones. The pair had siphoned roughly 10 million yen (around $63,000) using victims' stolen cards since 2024. Investigators are still trying to determine whether the 74 devices recovered are all their hardware, or whether more phones were used.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Seven shot dead by gunmen at church funeral in Jordan, state media say
articles.summary: Another 10 people are injured in the southern Karak governorate, and a manhunt is now under way.
articles.body:
At least seven people were killed when two gunmen opened fire on a funeral in central Jordan, the country's state media report.

Another 10 people were injured in the church in the Karak governorate on Friday.

The unidentified gunmen are reported to have arrived in a car and began shooting inside the church before fleeing the scene.

Security forces have been deployed to the area after the "heinous" attack, government spokesman Mohammad al-Momani said.

Dozens of people had been inside the church for the funeral when the shooting began, Khaled Burqan, one of the mourners, told Jordan's al-Mamlaka state-run TV.

He said the two attackers armed with a rifle and a pistol had been firing at the mourners for several minutes.

No-one has so far claimed responsibility for the attack.

A news briefing by interior ministry officials is expected shortly.

Karak has a sizeable Christian community in the majority-Muslim Jordan.

articles.title: At 14, Nepali schoolgirl Prakriti Malla went viral for her handwriting; one school assignment looked so perfect, people thought it was digitally printed
articles.summary: While we are in an age when children learn to type on keyboards and communicate through smartphones, Prakriti Malla, 16-year-old from Nepal, has gone
articles.body: While we are in an age when children learn to type on keyboards and communicate through smartphones, Prakriti Malla, 16-year-old from Nepal, has gone viral for her beyond perfect handwriting. People often mistook her handwriting for a computer font as the letters are so evenly shaped and so aptly spaced. It’s hard to believe that a young schoolgirl had written it by hand.According to information mentioned on Study International, October 19, 2017, Malla was just 14 years old and studying in Grade 8 at Birendra Sainik Awasiya Mahavidyalaya when her handwriting caught global attention in 2017. What began as an example of schoolwork soon became a viral sensation.When a school assignment went viralA page of English writing done by Malla became the centre of attention far beyond her classroom. Photographs of her work began circulating on social media and soon the pictures went viral. Her letters looked almost printed, with consistent shapes, carefully maintained spacing and a uniform appearance across the page.Some social media users even suggested that her handwriting could be turned into a computer font. It was so perfect.According to Study International's 2017 report, Malla had already attracted national recognition in Nepal in 2016. Her handwriting later travelled across international social media, introducing her unusual talent to a much wider audience.World's most beautiful “handwriting'The phrase 'world's most beautiful handwriting' soon became closely associated with her name. What is beyond doubt is the extraordinary attention her penmanship received.A talent recognised by UAEIn December 2022, Malla's penmanship received another international spotlight when she wrote a congratulatory letter to the leadership and people of the United Arab Emirates on the occasion of the country's 51st Spirit of the Union celebrations.She presented the handwritten message to the UAE Embassy in Nepal. The embassy acknowledged her contribution publicly, describing her in connection with the distinction of having the world's best handwriting.The discipline behind every letterMalla's writing stood out because rather than relying on elaborate decorative flourishes, her work impressed viewers through its balance and clarity. Each letter seemed to belong naturally in the line, while the spacing gave the page an almost typeset appearance.It would be easy to describe her talent simply as a natural gift.Why handwriting still matters in a digital worldMalla's story became inspiring because it emerged at a time when digital communication was becoming an increasingly ordinary part of everyday life. Typing offers speed, convenience and uniformity. Handwriting, by contrast, carries the physical imprint of the person holding the pen. A handwritten note can communicate care and emotions through the time taken to compose it.Her story also offers a refreshing perspective on what it means to become known online. She did not need a celebrity platform or an elaborate campaign to attract attention. A photograph of an ordinary school assignment was enough to make people pause, look closer and share what they saw.The image travelled because it surprised people.More than a viral photographYears after her schoolwork first attracted international attention, Prakriti Malla remains associated with an unusual achievement: making handwriting itself a subject of fascination.Her story is not merely about having neat letters. It is about how an everyday skill can become extraordinary when pursued with love and care. In a world that increasingly prizes speed, Malla's handwriting offered a different kind of appeal. It invited people to slow down and appreciate the details: the shape of a letter, the distance between two words and the balance of a line.Perhaps that is why her school assignment continues to capture attention. It represents a simple but enduring idea: even in a digital age, there is still something special about what human hands can create.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi or Varun Chakravarthy? Exploring India's potential XI for 2nd T20I vs NZ at Christchurch
articles.summary: India predicted playing XI for 2nd T20I vs NZ: With Ishan Kishan injured, will 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi debut, or will Varun Chakravarthy get a look...
articles.body:
India ace Ishan Kishan is out of the second T20I with a low-grade adductor strain.

Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is a leading option, but Varun Chakravarthy could also come in.

India lead the five-match series 1-0 ahead of Saturday's second game at Hagley Oval.

Will Varun Chakravarthy get the nod ahead of Vaibhav Sooryavanshi? Predicting India's playing XI for 2nd T20I vs New Zealand

India must now choose between a teenage batting prodigy and a proven spinner after an injury to Ishan Kishan opened up a spot in the side.

The wicketkeeper-batter will miss the second T20I against New Zealand at Hagley Oval in Christchurch on Saturday, and the team management is weighing its options after a record-breaking chase in the series opener.

The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) has confirmed that Kishan suffered a low-grade right adductor strain during the first T20I. Its medical team is monitoring his progress, but he will not be available as India try to stretch their 1-0 lead in the five-match series.

His absence matters because he was part of the batting group that had been reshuffled for the opening game, where he was dismissed for one off three balls.

Vaibhav Sooryavanshi was in the squad but sat out the first match, and he is now one of the obvious candidates to replace Kishan. The 15-year-old has already made his senior international debut, and he was part of the gold-medal-winning men's cricket team at the 2026 Asian Games.

Picking him would therefore mean a return to the playing XI, which has been a talking point among fans for several matches.

Speaking about Sooryavanshi, batting coach Sitanshu Kotak said, "If Ishan doesn't play, unless he recovers completely, which the medical team will advise, Vaibhav could definitely step in for him. He is one of the strongest contenders."

The decision is not as simple as swapping one batter for another. According to Revsportz , India could surprise people by going in a different direction and might prefer an extra bowling option in Varun Chakravarthy.

If Sooryavanshi does come in, the order at the top becomes the next question. One is Sanju Samson, Abhishek Sharma and Sooryavanshi in that order, another is Abhishek, Sooryavanshi and Samson.

India predicted XI vs New Zealand for 2nd T20I at Christchurch

This is a prediction built from the side that played the first T20I, with Sooryavanshi replacing Kishan. Chakravarthy would come in at the expense of one of the batters if the management chooses extra bowling.

India should pick Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, but the balance of the side still matters

The case for playing Sooryavanshi is strong, and not only because of his talent. He has sat out six consecutive matches, the team has just lost a batter, and an injury is the cleanest way to give a young player a game without dropping a set opener. Fans have wanted this for a while, and there is little downside in trying him in a series that India already lead.

However, Chakravarthy's case deserves a hearing. India's bowling attack is a lighter unit than usual, and a spinner like Chakravarthy could be a handy option. The best answer may depend on the pitch, which should be assessed on match day.

Ideally, India would play Sooryavanshi and keep their bowling resources intact by resting a batter lower down the order, since Dhir and Reddy both bring some depth. Whatever the final call, the management should avoid treating the teenager as a stopgap. If he plays, he should get a clear role and a run of games, so the selection reads as a plan and not a reaction to an injury.

articles.title: UK govt urges households to keep 3 days of food and water for emergencies
articles.summary: The UK government has launched the 'Be Ready' campaign urging households to maintain three days' worth of food and water supplies in response to cyber threats and extreme weather. Prime Minister Andy Burnham emphasizes the importance of preparedness for emergencies.
articles.body: The UK government has urged households to keep three days of food and water at home, citing recent cyber disruptions and increasingly frequent extreme weather as reasons to prepare for emergencies.The advice was reinforced on Friday through the government's newly launched “Be Ready” campaign, which recommends storing bottled water and non-perishable food to help families cope if essential services are disrupted.Prime Minister Andy Burnham said recent events showed why Britain needed to improve its preparedness for crises rather than react after they occurred. Speaking at a meeting on the country's response to wildfires, he said the government had previously been “on the back foot” when dealing with emergencies.“Unexpected events seem to be becoming more and more common,” Burnham said, urging people to take practical steps to prepare for situations that could interrupt daily life.He stressed that the guidance was not intended to encourage panic buying.“It's not about panic buying... It's about just taking sensible measures to have enough in the house to tide you over should there be a difficult situation,” he said.The announcement follows a major cybersecurity incident involving vulnerabilities in PHP, a programming language used by websites and online services. The flaws were disclosed on Wednesday, prompting organisations around the world to review their systems. Some services were taken offline, while millions of hacking attempts were reported.Defence Secretary Wes Streeting warned that cyber incidents could become more frequent as artificial intelligence makes it easier for attackers to identify weaknesses in digital systems. He also pointed to threats from hostile states, organised criminals and climate change.Speaking on the BBC's Question Time, Streeting said the UK faced a level of threat “than we have certainly for most, if not all, of my lifetime”.Alongside cyber risks, the government is responding to extreme weather, including storms and a summer marked by record heat, drought and wildfires. Ministers have announced a new wildfire response plan that includes deploying military aircraft to support firefighting efforts.The government says the household guidance is intended to help people manage temporary disruptions caused by events such as war, cyberattacks or natural disasters.The advice is similar to a recommendation issued by the European Commission last year, which encouraged people across the European Union to maintain a 72-hour emergency kit containing essentials such as food, water, cash and power banks.You use AI every day.
